title: Spec Engine — Codegen Manifest Contract
description: Machine-checkable form of the PER-MODULE honesty ledger `spec_engine.codegen.generate_app()` writes to `.spec-engine/codegen-manifest.json` in a generated app's repo, alongside `.spec-engine/scaffold-plan.json`. The parent `ScaffoldPlan.codegen_status` is one top-level enum (`not_started` | `generated`) and cannot express that a 'generated' plan mixes fully-real modules with labeled stubs — THIS file is where that mix is recorded, per module, machine-checkably: 'generated' (real, working code — e.g. backend-model CRUD stores, frontend-page renderers, the acceptance test suite), 'generated-stub-logic' (the module's wiring/entry-point is real and executes, but its business-logic body is a documented placeholder — e.g. a flow's step sequence), or 'stub' (a labeled placeholder only — e.g. a third-party integration connector codegen cannot wire without real credentials/API contract). Same load-bearing-labels discipline TESS-VISION-AND-BUILD-SPEC.html applies everywhere: 'do not silently upgrade a label.'

codegen_status.description: Always 'generated' — this manifest only exists once codegen.generate_app() has actually run; a 'not_started' plan has no manifest file.

module_id.description: Matches the module_id in the sibling scaffold-plan.json — traceability between the plan and what was actually written.

generation_status.description: 'generated-connector' (Connectors v1, docs/design/connectors-architecture.md §6.3) is an ADDITIVE fourth value: real client code generated from a REGISTERED connector manifest, operational once its declared env var is configured — deliberately distinct from plain 'generated' because operability depends on runtime configuration this repo cannot carry.

connector.description: Non-null ONLY on a 'generated-connector' entry: connector id@version, manifest content hash, the operations wired, the declared env var names, and the side-effect classes — the exact surface the approval gate's content hash (spec_engine.content.plan_content_hash) is bound to. Always present as a key (null on every other generation_status) so this schema can require it uniformly.

infrastructure_files.description: Files written by codegen that are required scaffolding for the target stack but are NOT derived from any single spec section (e.g. src/server.js, src/http-util.js, package.json) — kept separate from `modules` so traceability back to the spec stays honest: only `modules[].files` claim a `source_section`.

$comment: Minimal-validator keyword subset supported by spec_engine.spec_check: type, enum, properties, required, additionalProperties, items.
